problem: Call a 9-digit number a cassowary if it uses each of the digits 1 through 9 exactly once. Compute the number of cassowaries that are prime.
solution: Every cassowary is divisible by 3, as the sum of its digits is $1 + 2 + 	ext{···} + 9 = 45$. Since all such numbers are divisible by 3 and greater than 3, none of them are prime. So, there are 0 prime cassowaries.
